title: Etale near a point from smoothness and zero fibre dimension there
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], $x\in X$, $s=f(x)$, $\kappa(s)$ its residue field [def-weil-residue-field] and $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ the fibre [def-pc-base-change]. Assume that there is an open subscheme $U\subseteq X$ with $x\in U$ such that $f|_U:U\to S$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and that the dimension of $X_s$ at the point corresponding to $x$ is $0$ [def-kun-dimension]. Then there is an open subscheme $U'\subseteq U$ with $x\in U'$ such that $f|_{U'}:U'\to S$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism].

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 0A43 (label lemma-check-smoothness-on-infinitesimal-nbhds), proof, last sentence ('Part (2) follows from (1) and the fact that a morphism is etale if and only if it is smooth of relative dimension 0'); with morphisms.tex: remark after Definition 02GI (line 8079), Lemma 02G1 (lemma-smooth-omega-finite-locally-free: Omega_{X/S} finite locally free of rank dim_x(X_{f(x)}) for f smooth) and Definition 02G2 (definition-smooth-relative-dimension)

proof.text: (The fibre of $f|_U$ has dimension $0$ at $x$.) Let $p:X_s\to X$, $q:X_s\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ be the projections and $x'\in X_s$ the point corresponding to $x$; since $p$ is a homeomorphism onto $f^{-1}(s)\ni x$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre], $x'$ is the unique point of $X_s$ with $p(x')=x$. Likewise let $U_s=U\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ be the fibre of $f|_U$ over $s$ [def-pc-base-change], with projections $p_U,q_U$, and $x'_U$ the unique point of $U_s$ with $p_U(x'_U)=x$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] to $f$ and $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to S$ with the open subschemes $U\subseteq X$, $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ (all of it) and $S$ (all of it): the canonical morphism $j:U_s\to X_s$ is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] with image $p^{-1}(U)$, and $p\circ j=p_U$ followed by the inclusion $U\subseteq X$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Hence $p(j(x'_U))=x$, so $j(x'_U)=x'$, and $j$ is a homeomorphism of $U_s$ onto the open subspace $p^{-1}(U)$ of $X_s$ sending $x'_U$ to $x'$. A homeomorphism carries open neighbourhoods to open neighbourhoods and chains of irreducible closed subsets to chains of the same length, so $\dim_{x'_U}(U_s)=\dim_{x'}(p^{-1}(U))$ [def-kun-dimension, def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point]. By [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-open-subspace] with $Y=X_s$, $O=p^{-1}(U)$, $y=x'$, this equals $\dim_{x'}(X_s)$, which is $0$ by hypothesis. So $\dim_{x'_U}(U_s)=0$.

source.place: Topology, Definition 0055 (definition-Krull, line 1392) and the remark after it (line 1421: dimension at a point is computed on arbitrarily small open neighbourhoods); fibres of open subschemes as open subschemes of the fibre: schemes.tex, Lemma 01K1 (lemma-fibre-topological) for the points of the fibre

proof.text: (The differentials vanish near $x$.) The morphism $f|_U:U\to S$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and $x\in U$. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-differentials-free-rank-fibre-dimension] applied to $f|_U$ and $x$ there are affine open subschemes $V\subseteq S$ and $W\subseteq U$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] with $x\in W$ and $f(W)\subseteq V$ such that, with $R=\mathcal O_S(V)$, $A=\mathcal O_U(W)$ and $R\to A$ the ring map of $f|_W:W\to V$, the module $\Omega_{A/R}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] is free of rank $\dim_{x'_U}(U_s)$, which is $0$ by step 1. A free module of rank $0$ is the zero module, so $\Omega_{A/R}=0$.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 02G1 (lemma-smooth-omega-finite-locally-free, line 7214: Omega_{X/S} finite locally free of rank dim_x(X_{f(x)})), with Lemma 01UT (lemma-differentials-affine) on the affine open W

proof.text: (Etale near $x$.) By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-zero-differentials-affine-open-etale] applied to the smooth morphism $g=f|_U:U\to S$ and the affine opens $V$, $W$ of step 2 (with $\Omega_{A/R}=0$), the restriction $g|_W=f|_W:W\to S$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. As $W$ is open in $U$ and $U$ is open in $X$, $U':=W$ is an open subscheme of $X$ with $x\in U'\subseteq U$ and $f|_{U'}$ etale.
